direction_as_read: Positive on LDL-C and total cholesterol in small, sponsor-funded trials of specific branded extracts at 375 to 400 mg, with no clinical outcomes; a 2026 meta-analysis grades the evidence low to very low certainty
summary: All five labels print a generic bergamot fruit extract at 500 or 1000 mg with cardiovascular, lipid or metabolic purposes, and none prints a flavonoid amount. Two Bionap-funded placebo trials of Bergavit 375 mg/day, about 150 mg/day flavonoids, named LDL-C and total cholesterol as primary endpoints and found between-group reductions (39682955, 42592560); HDL-C didn't differ. Brumex 400 mg and Endoberg also lowered lipids, but those abstracts name no primary outcome (37312672, 37732063). A 2026 meta-analysis found low to very low certainty and says its results should not be read as establishing clinical efficacy (42746152). A 25% bergamot juice drink showed no between-arm difference in healthy adults (38767145).
question_for_clinician: 39682955 and 42592560 meet rule 2 for Bergavit at 375 mg/day, both positive on named primary lipid endpoints. Should these labels get credit, given they print a generic extract with no flavonoid amount, the trials tested one juice-derived extract standardized to 150 mg/day flavonoids, Bionap funded both trials, and the outcomes are surrogates? Agent recommendation: no credit in this review, because the labels can't be shown to contain the tested extract.

outcomes.name: LDL-C: 11.5% decrease at 4 months on active, 2.2% increase on placebo; between-group difference significant at months 3 and 4
Total cholesterol: 8.8% decrease at 4 months; between-group difference significant at months 3 and 4
Oxidized LDL and PON1 activity: between-group difference at month 4 only; oxidized LDL had no significant within-group trend

limitations: Five endpoints are named primary; the full text passages read don't name a correction for that.

A Bionap employee is an author and the data are not publicly available; the authors say the funder had no role in design, analysis or writing.
Diet wasn't monitored and there was no post-intervention follow-up, per the authors.
Surrogate lipid markers only, no clinical events.
